composition_parti.rule: The facade is near-symmetrical, not strict-bilateral: openings are located by the rooms behind them and then nudged toward apparent balance, so exact symmetry is a frequent outcome rather than a governing rule.
composition_parti.note: Overrides the cascade's inherited strict-bilateral-odd-bay (via colonial-revival's own family, eclectic-revivals), which is the wrong composition mode for this node: the style's own governing_logic states plainly 'nothing is derived from a module of order' and that apparent rhythm is a residual of plan-driven openings, not a designed symmetry system.

variants.note: The FHA's most-published elevation and Levitt's chosen form (cape-cod-massing, canonical massing affinity).
Named directly in defining_characteristics: 'gabled or hipped.'
The single-storey version with a projecting entry or living-room gable, the one compositional move the style allows itself (massing_affinities, common).
Overrides the cascade's inherited value (shingle-style, via colonial-revival's family). No source names a gambrel roof for this node; the roof is a simple gable or hip throughout.

roof_form.rule: Compact rectangular or shallow-L massing under a simple gable or hip roof, one storey or one and a half. No secondary roof form of any complexity.
roof_form.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 1-2. Fixes a cascade bug: the resolved kit previously inherited 'gambrel' from shingle-style (spliced in via colonial-revival's own family, eclectic-revivals), which contradicts this node's own stated roof forms.

roof_pitch.rule: Roof pitch 4:12 to 6:12 -- a hard constraint (c02) and a repeated figure in typical_ratios.
roof_pitch.note: Fixes a cascade bug: the resolved kit previously inherited 'pitch_min=9:12' from queen-anne-american (spliced in via colonial-revival's own family), which is nearly double this node's own documented ceiling and directly contradicts its own hard constraint c02.

roof_material.rule: Low-fired clay barrel tile (the cascade's inherited value from mediterranean-vernacular, spliced in via a distant family branch) has no basis anywhere in this node's own text or lineage and is climatically and economically wrong for an FHA production house of the 1930s-1950s in climate zones 2-6.
roof_material.note: Forbidding only, not specifying a replacement: the node's own text never names a roofing material directly, so asserting one (asphalt composition shingle is the well-known historical answer) would be an unsourced positive claim. Marked judgment because the forbidding itself is inferred from context (region, era, cost-engineering) rather than from an explicit statement.

eave_condition.rule: Eave and rake overhang not exceeding 12 in and frequently under 6 in, closed tight to the wall plane with no bracket, rafter tail, or purlin end -- 'a recognizably traditional shape with essentially no eave... the roof surface stops at the wall surface and the two meet without a shadow line' (diagnostic_tells).
eave_condition.note: Fixes a cascade bug: the resolved kit previously inherited shingle-style's eave rule verbatim (spliced in via colonial-revival's own family), which happens to share the same 12 in ceiling by coincidence but is sourced from an unrelated style and omits this node's own, far more diagnostic point -- that the overhang is frequently zero and the wall meets the sky with no shadow at all.

variants.note: distinguished_from[0] reads 'The tell is the rake: a Cape Cod Revival has a moulded rake with a return at the eave; Minimal Traditional has a 1x6 board.', and this kit's own `cornice_return`, bound forbidden, reads 'No cornice return of any consequence; the rake is a plain board, not a moulded rake returned at the eave'.

rake_trim_width_in.source: proportions/systems/trim-craftsman.json -- the stock series its module note states: '1x6 (5 1/2)'
rake_trim_width_in.note: 'Minimal Traditional has a 1x6 board.' (distinguished_from[0]). A dressed 1x6 is 5 1/2 in, as trim-craftsman, which this node binds itself, states ('1x6 (5 1/2)'), on Lucas's answer B29 of 1 Oct 2026, which supersedes B10's nominal 6 in; craftsman's head casing has carried the same dressed figure from the same pack since WP-14.5.

rake_condition.rule: minimal-traditional's rake is a plain board, a 1x6, with no moulding and no return, under an eave and rake overhang not exceeding 12 in and frequently under 6 in (c01; this kit's `eave_condition`).
rake_condition.note: BOUND 1 Oct 2026 (WP-16.9), on Lucas's answer B5 of 30 Sep 2026, recorded in oq/the-rake-is-drawn-as-an-edge-and-carries-no-member: the companion of colonial-revival's own `rake_condition` binding of the same date, which permits a boxed rake with a return and would otherwise reach this node by descent (lineage[0], `descends_from`). Until then this slot was `open` and resolved ELIZABETHAN's record, 'No exposed gable verge in the ordinary sense; the roofline terminates at the parapet, not at a projecting gable rake.', reached at position 25 of this node's cascade; none of the 24 nodes before it binds the slot. This node's own words state its rake, and it is a gable's: defining_characteristics[1] reads 'Moderate roof pitch of 4:12 to 6:12, gabled or hipped, with eave and rake overhang not exceeding 12 in and frequently under 6 in', c01 'Eave and rake overhang shall not exceed 12 in.', and distinguished_from[0] 'The tell is the rake: a Cape Cod Revival has a moulded rake with a return at the eave; Minimal Traditional has a 1x6 board.' The record names no parapet. The overhang is c01's one figure for eave and rake, which this kit's `eave_condition` already carries (`overhang_max_in`, 12 in, source minimal-traditional.c01); it is not restated here. The board's width is the dressed 1x6, 5 1/2 in, measured from trim-craftsman's stock series, on Lucas's answer B29 of 1 Oct 2026; B10 of 30 Sep had taken the nominal 6 in on a false premise (that no record here states the dressed width), and was asked again. The fault this slot answers excepts this node ('0-12 in on both eave and rake is the type'); Lucas's answer B3 keeps an excepted style's edge, and his answer B10 of 30 Sep 2026 settles this node: B5's kit-first governs an excepted style whose own kit states its rake, so its gable end draws its own board; B29 fixes its width at 5 1/2 in. The rule names this node because three nodes descend through it, ranch-style, neo-eclectic and modern-farmhouse-traditional, and two of them state other rakes: ranch-style's c03 'eave and rake overhang between 18 and 36 in', and modern-farmhouse-traditional's c02 'Rake overhang not less than 8 in and eave overhang not less than 12 in, with a returned or moulded termination at every gable corner.' Those two bind records of their own of the same date (T1, taken as recommended under Lucas's standing instruction of 1 Oct 2026: put to him and unanswered when the instruction arrived), and neo-eclectic's cascade reaches ranch-style's record before this one, so no node inherits this record. None of the three is drawn. The address stays governed by `opening-pointed`, bound on gothic-revival-british (`part * 3.5`) -- OQ 51's delivery, not endorsed, and unchanged by this binding.

cornice_return.rule: No cornice return of any consequence; the rake is a plain board, not a moulded rake returned at the eave (defining_characteristics[4]; distinguished_from cape-cod-revival).
cornice_return.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2) as the companion of colonial-revival's own `cornice_return` binding of the same date, which permits a return and would otherwise reach this node by descent. Until then this slot was `open` and resolved gothic-revival-american's `forbidden` binding through colonial-revival: the right outcome, on a bargeboard reason that is not this node's. Its own words: defining_characteristics[4] reads 'Trim of minimal profile depth — flat frieze, narrow clamshell or ranch casing, no cornice return of any consequence'; distinguished_from[0] (cape-cod-revival) reads 'The tell is the rake: a Cape Cod Revival has a moulded rake with a return at the eave; Minimal Traditional has a 1x6 board.'; and this kit's own `trim_family` rule already ends 'and no cornice return of any consequence'. The words 'of any consequence' leave a vestigial stub unstated; the return the elevation draws is a full one, which the record rules out.

gable_treatment.rule: A single small gabled or hipped entry projection or bay is permitted as the only three-dimensional event on the whole elevation; anything more is outside the node.

variants.note: A later, non-original expansion of the attic on one-and-a-half storey examples, not part of the style's original vocabulary.

dormer.rule: Dormers are not part of the original design vocabulary; where one appears on a one-and-a-half storey example it is a shed dormer added at the rear in a later remodel, not an original feature.

belt_course.rule: No belt course: ornament is reduced to three items at most, none of them a belt, on a house of one storey or one and a half.
belt_course.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), the companion of colonial-revival's own `belt_course` binding of the same date, which permits a belt course and would otherwise reach this node by descent: this node descends from colonial-revival directly (lineage[0]), and mid-century-traditional, the family the cascade walks first, binds nothing at this slot. Until then this slot was `open` and resolved shingle-style's `forbidden` binding through colonial-revival: the right outcome, on a reason that is not this node's. Its own words: defining_characteristics[3] reads 'Ornament reduced to three items at most: a chimney, a pair of decorative shutters, and a simple door surround', and c02 reads 'one or one and a half storeys only.' Marked judgment: the record names no belt, and the ban is read from its ornament cap and its storey count.

variants.note: defining_characteristics[3] budgets the ornament: 'Ornament reduced to three items at most: a chimney, a pair of decorative shutters, and a simple door surround'. A modillion course is not one of the three, and lineage[0] names what did not survive the descent from colonial-revival: 'the proportional system, the trim profiles, and the applied orders do not'.
The same count: 'Ornament reduced to three items at most: a chimney, a pair of decorative shutters, and a simple door surround'.

cornice.rule: No modillioned or dentilled cornice: the trim is of minimal profile depth and the ornament is budgeted at three named items (defining_characteristics[3] and [4]).
cornice.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2) as the companion of colonial-revival's own `cornice` binding of the same date, which makes `modillion-cornice` canonical and would otherwise reach this node by descent. Until then this slot was `open` and resolved gothic-revival-british's record through colonial-revival: the right refusal of the modillion cornice, for c05's reason rather than this node's, with a corbelled brick cornice canonical and colonial-revival's 12-18 in cornice depth merged in. This node's own words: defining_characteristics[4] reads 'Trim of minimal profile depth — flat frieze, narrow clamshell or ranch casing, no cornice return of any consequence'; diagnostic_tells[0] reads 'A recognizably traditional shape with essentially no eave — the roof surface stops at the wall surface and the two meet without a shadow line'. No variant is made canonical: the long description gives the eave 'a flat frieze board' and no cornice variant in the corpus plainly matches it.

variants.note: defining_characteristics[4]: 'Trim of minimal profile depth — flat frieze, narrow clamshell or ranch casing, no cornice return of any consequence'; description.long: 'The trim is a two-and-a-quarter-inch clamshell casing and a flat frieze board.'

frieze.rule: A flat frieze board of minimal profile depth -- with the clamshell casing, the whole of the trim minimal-traditional's own description.long names: 'The trim is a two-and-a-quarter-inch clamshell casing and a flat frieze board.'
frieze.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), and it was FORBIDDEN here until then -- inherited, on 'No frieze board may interrupt the shingle field.', from SHINGLE-STYLE. This node's own record names the member twice -- description.long, 'The trim is a two-and-a-quarter-inch clamshell casing and a flat frieze board.', and defining_characteristics[4], 'Trim of minimal profile depth — flat frieze, narrow clamshell or ranch casing, no cornice return of any consequence' -- and this kit's trim_family rule repeats it: 'Trim of minimal profile depth: flat frieze board, narrow clamshell or ranch casing'. A style does not list a member it forbids as one of its only two trims. No depth is stated for the board, so this record carries no figure -- and the cascade then supplies one, from an order: with the ban lifted, precedence gives the slot to `palladio-ionic` (bound on english-palladian, storey_height / 4 * (6 / 18)), the delivery that already governs this node's `cornice`, against this node's own governing_logic, 'Nothing is derived from a module of order' -- the sentence it declined `gibbs-ionic` and `chambers-ionic` on. Its `chambers-ionic` decline already says so: 'palladio-ionic and benjamin-ionic on this node are the next adjudications.' ranch-style, neo-eclectic and modern-farmhouse-traditional, which inherit this record and decline `palladio-ionic`, take `palladio-tuscan` (bound on italian-renaissance) at this slot instead. OQ 51's delivery, counted and not endorsed. The rule names this node, so that in their resolved records it does not describe their trim as a clamshell casing.

variants.note: Overrides the cascade's inherited value (georgian-colonial-american, via colonial-revival's family). A door this elaborate contradicts the node's own description of a budget-permitting 'simple door surround' at most.

entry_door.rule: The door itself carries no ornament beyond, at most, a simple applied surround if the budget allowed; it sits in the plane of the wall with a reveal of an inch or less and no projecting surround.
entry_door.note: Direct quote of the long description ('a simple door surround') and diagnostic_tells item 3. Fixes a cascade bug: the previously-resolved six-panel raised-and-fielded door is Georgian-Colonial-American's own high-style door, wholly inconsistent with this node's cost-engineered minimalism.

door_surround.rule: No projecting classical surround of any kind. The door lies in the plane of the wall with a reveal of an inch or less; a pilasters-and-entablature treatment (the cascade's inherited value) is exactly the kind of expensive, cost-engineered-out element this style deleted first.
door_surround.note: Direct quote of diagnostic_tells item 3 ('the front door lies in the plane of the wall with a reveal of an inch or less and no projecting surround'). Fixes a cascade bug: the previously-resolved pilasters-and-entablature surround is inherited from english-georgian/colonial-revival via the family splice and directly contradicts this diagnostic.

variants.note: The record closes the question by counting: 'Ornament reduced to three items at most: a chimney, a pair of decorative shutters, and a simple door surround.' A fanlight is a fourth item. Its diagnostic tell says the same from the other side: 'The front door lies in the plane of the wall with a reveal of an inch or less and no projecting surround.'
A door in the plane of the wall with no projecting surround has nowhere to put a transom bar. Possible on a deeper-walled example and not what the style is.

The style's ornament budget is three items and they are named. An elliptical fanlight is the Colonial Revival's most expensive single gesture, and this style is defined against exactly that expense -- it is the Depression-era reduction OF the revival.
Same count, same reason. Sidelights widen the entry assembly beyond 'a simple door surround', which the record fixes as the whole of the entry's ornament.

transom_sidelight.note: BOUND 28 Aug 2026 by WP-8.4's own adversarial audit, which measured what the `colonial-revival` binding earlier in this session PROPAGATED. That binding is right for its own node and reaches ten descendants by descent, carrying `elliptical-fanlight` and `sidelights` CANONICAL to three whose own records contradict it -- and it is not inert: `elevation.py:318` reads `sidelights_forbidden` off exactly this resolved binding, so the generator began DRAWING an Adamesque fanlight-and-sidelight entry on these houses. The prior state was not right either: the slot was `open`, so it resolved through `colonial-revival` to GOTHIC-REVIVAL-BRITISH's blanket prohibition. Two wrong answers, and this is the node's own. OQ 87's mechanism -- `resolve_slots` stops its walk only on `specified` or `forbidden`, so a slot bound `open` inherits its nearest ancestor's record in full. The node's own defining characteristic budgets ornament at three named items and a fanlight is not one of them.

variants.note: This node's own, actually-built answer: 'a detached garage at the rear of the lot, reached by a driveway beside the house' (distinguished_from vs ranch-style). Retrieved from documented practice, not invented -- Minimal Traditional predates the attached-garage problem the rest of the family exists to solve.

Where the type is reproduced on a modern infill lot without room for a detached rear garage, the family's own 4 ft-setback / 33-percent-width answer (mid-century-traditional.garage_strategy) applies. This half of the entry is an editorial extension for contemporary buildability, not a historical fact about the 1930s-50s house.

garage_strategy.rule: The type's own historical answer to the garage predates the problem the rest of the family exists to solve: keep it detached at the rear of the lot. A contemporary reproduction on a lot too narrow for that reverts to the family's later, invented answer.

edit_provenance.note: The canonical variant is retrieved directly from the node's own text, not invented -- unlike ranch-style and neo-eclectic, Minimal Traditional's garage is a solved problem by its own account. The permitted contemporary-infill variant is an honest editorial addition, flagged as such rather than presented as period fact.

porch_type.rule: No full- or partial-width habitable porch (hard constraint c04, soft severity on the entry-cover-projection number). Entry is a stoop, at most under a small hood or shallow entry gable, with cover projection not more than 3 ft.
porch_type.note: Direct quote of minimal-traditional.c04 and defining_characteristics item 3.

steps_and_stoop.rule: Entry is a plain stoop, occasionally under a small hood; there is nowhere to stand out of the rain beyond it.
steps_and_stoop.note: Direct quote of the long description's own summary of the style's felt experience ('there is nowhere to stand out of the rain').

variants.note: Overrides the cascade's inherited value (english-georgian, via colonial-revival's family). This node's whole point is the absence of a classical-depth trim system.

trim_family.rule: Trim of minimal profile depth: flat frieze board, narrow clamshell or ranch casing (2 1/4 in wide, under 3/4 in projection -- see the already-specified `casing` slot), and no cornice return of any consequence.
trim_family.note: Direct quote of defining_characteristics item 5. Fixes a cascade bug: english-georgian's real, deep classical trim system (gibbsian-bolection) is inherited via the family splice and is precisely what this style deleted.

circulation_parti.rule: A cellular plan of small, individually-walled rooms rather than an open or flowing plan; circulation is not itself a compositional device.
circulation_parti.note: Direct quote of distinguished_from[ranch-style] ('Minimal Traditional is an upright compact block with a cellular plan'). Marked judgment because the node's own text names the plan type in passing, in a comparison to another node, rather than describing it directly as its own subject.
